info.title: CRM Platform API
info.description:
The CRM platform API. One versioned REST surface: the web app, the mobile app,
the public API and partner integrations are all clients of exactly this, and there
are no hidden internal endpoints (ADR-0007).

## Authentication

Every endpoint requires a session except liveness, readiness and this document
itself. A browser authenticates with the httpOnly session cookie set at sign-in;
every other client sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A user who belongs to
more than one workspace may name one with `X-Tenant-Id` — that is a request, not
an authorization: the server checks the membership and derives the tenant from the
session either way (CLAUDE.md §5.2).

A handful of routes are reachable without a session because they cannot have one
yet — sign-up, sign-in, the MFA second step, email verification, the password-reset
pair, Google sign-in, and invitation acceptance. They are not unauthenticated: the
one-time token in the link or body *is* the credential, and it is checked against
its own row (ADR-0019). They are marked `security: []` below.

## Envelopes

Every success is `{ data, meta }`; every failure is `{ error: { code, message,
details, requestId } }` with a stable, machine-readable `code`. Codes may be added
to, never renamed. Every response carries `X-Request-Id`; quote it when reporting a
problem.

## Paging

Lists are keyset-paginated (ADR-0012): pass `meta.nextCursor` back as `cursor`.
There is no `page` or `offset`. The cursor is opaque — never parse or construct one.

## Versioning

Within `/api/v1`, changes are additive only. Anything breaking gets `/api/v2`.

## How this document is produced

Generated from the Zod schemas in `packages/contracts`, which are the same schemas
the API validates with — so it cannot drift from what the server accepts. Rules that
JSON Schema cannot express (for example "these two query parameters must be given
together") are stated in prose on the operation and enforced by the API regardless.

post.summary: Attach a file to a record: declare it, get a place to upload it
post.description: Creates the row and returns a **presigned upload URL**. The file goes from the browser straight to object storage and never through this API (CLAUDE.md §5.12). The content type is decided here from the allow-listed extension — never taken from the client — and bound into the signature along with the exact size. The storage key is random and is never returned. Requires `update` on the record the file is being attached to, which is also what makes a record in another tenant, or outside the caller scope, a 404.

post.summary: Edit, assign, delete or tag many records at once
post.description: At most 200 records per call, named by id or chosen by a list filter (a `nextCursor` comes back when more match; send it as `after`). One transaction; each record is attempted on its own, so one that cannot be changed is skipped and reported and the rest still go through, while an unexpected failure rolls the whole call back. Every record is held to what a single edit or delete holds it to: `can()` with its owner, field-level write permission, the version check, an audit entry and an outbox event. `skipped[].reason`: `not_found` covers a missing, deleted, other-tenant or out-of-scope id alike (it never says which); `not_permitted` is said only of a record the caller can see. Bulk edit may only change a short list of fields plus active custom fields. `dryRun` reports without changing anything. Accepts an `Idempotency-Key` header: a retry returns the stored answer with `replayed: true`.

The body is `application/json`, at most 16 KB, and is checked against a strict schema **built from the form's own fields** plus `consent` (must be `true`), `fillToken` (from the definition) and the hidden `website_url` (must be empty): any other key is a 422. Accepts an `Idempotency-Key` header (1 to 128 of letters, digits and `_ . : -`); a repeat with the same key answers the same and makes no second lead. Every accepted outcome answers `{ received: true }` and nothing more, so the answer never reveals whether the visitor matched an existing record. A page submitted within three seconds of being drawn, or more than four hours after, answers 422 `FORM_EXPIRED`. One of the only two routes in the API that need no session, and the only ones a stranger can write through (ADR-0065; the `PUBLIC_ROUTES` list in the test suite keeps the set closed). The key in the path selects the workspace and the form; nothing the caller sends can. A wrong key, a revoked key, a disabled form, a paused workspace and a withdrawn feature all answer the same 404. No cookie is read or set, there is no CORS approval, and the query string must be empty.
